title: 9x9 transformer-based KataGo: full self-play training loop on the Schmidt B200/B300 cluster

models.jobs: fable xhigh   (decompose, design, DAG reformulation, escalation)
models.worker: opus max     (acquire, build, code, run, ledger appends)
models.refuter: fable high  (cross-model: never the worker's model)

externalReviewers.codex: gpt-5.6-sol at model_reasoning_effort=xhigh via `codex exec`; owns the second giant-DAG pass and one seat of the two-model DAG review

sources.ref-paper: arxiv-1902.10565  (Wu, Accelerating Self-Play Learning in Go)

compute.cpuPolicy: no CPU usage limit (human decision 2026-09-03); jobs still declare --cpus-per-task honestly

gitPolicy.branch: az: main (consumer artifacts) · phys-agentic-loop: ssci (framework changes)

layout.consumerRepo: az (this repo, branch main) — results/, progress/, ref-code/, ref-paper/, mission.json tracked here
layout.framework: phys-agentic-loop/ submodule, branch ssci — methodology source only; ledger CLIs are run from the az root: python3 phys-agentic-loop/_common/<ledger>.py …

sourcePriority.primary: ref-code/lightvector-KataGo @ v1.18.2 (most recent release; master is +3 commits touching only OpenCL/poswriter/docs)
sourcePriority.background: ref-paper/arxiv-1902.10565 — 2019 paper, outdated; cite only where the current code still implements the idea
sourcePriority.note: paper id arxiv-1902.10565 stays as the ledger namespace label only

decisions.decision: no CPU usage limit; the 20% clause in PROMPT.md is withdrawn
scratch budget for selfplay data + checkpoints = 500 GiB
run on b200 while b300 is reserved; same GPU count
